In it, the portrait of Magdalen is based on the Marchesa Attavanti, sister of an escapee who hides in the chapel of Sant' Andrea della Valle and eventually takes poison after being captured in the well of the garden. "E lucevan le stelle" and "Recondita armonia" are sung by Angelloti's fellow Republican, the painter Mario Cavaradossi, whose mock execution on the roof of Fort St. Angelo becomes real after the stabbing of Scarpia causes the title character to leap to her death. Name this Puccini opera.

This author of Emil Kolb and Knulp criticized the educational system in Beneath the Wheel. In one of his novels, Franz Kromer taunts a boy who has falsely confessed to stealing apples, Emil Sinclair. In another, Plinio Designori's friend Joseph Knecht is awarded the title "Magister Ludi." In another, an incident in Pablo's hall of mirrors causes a sentence of "eternal life" to be pronounced on Harry Haller. Identify this author of Demian, The Glass Bead Game, Steppenwolf, and Siddhartha.

His nonfiction was collected in This Quiet Dust while the pieces "Love Day" and "Shadrach" appear in the short story collection A Tidewater Morning. He was a founder of the Paris Review and wrote such works about military life as In the Clap Shack and The Long March. He found more success with a 1979 story about a Virginia writer's relationship with a Polish Holocaust survivor and a chronicle of a slave revolt. Identify this author of Sophie's Choice and The Confessions of Nat Turner.

In one of this author's stories, The Boss tortures an insect with an ink blotter after recalling his son's death in World War I, and in another, Bertha Young cannot maintain the title emotion. In addition to "The Fly" and "Bliss," this former cellist who broke into writing with In a German Pension wrote "Marriage a la Mode," "At the Bay," and a story about Laura Sheridan's struggle with class distinctions. Name this New Zealand-based author of The Garden Party.

Without a leading article, this is the title of a poem that offers poets the chance to "pass the straits and conquer the mountains" and "double the Cape of Good Hope to some purpose." It exhorts the soul to "steer for the deep waters only" and to "farther, farther, farther sail." With its leading article, it is the title of a novel centering on Cyril Fielding's reaction to the ambiguous events between Adela Quested and Dr. Aziz. What is this almost-common title of a Walt Whitman poem and E.M. Forster novel?

His The Evidence of Things Not Seen deals with the Atlanta child murders of the early 1980s. As a youth, he spent his free time as a preacher, an experience incorporated into his play The Amen Corner, and he also wrote about the expatriate David, who is denied a job by Guillame. This author of The Fire Next Time and Giovanni's Room also wrote a novel about John Grimes's fourteenth birthday in Harlem. Name this writer of Go Tell It on the Mountain.

He is described as dying at the hands of Esau in Genesis 25 while trying to reclaim a garment that had belonged to Adam. That occurred on the same day as the death of Abraham, who is often contrasted with this man. Called "al- Jabbar" in Islam, the Bible describes this man as the first carnivore and says he defeated an army of Japethites to become king and pursue his best-known folly. Name this ruler of Sinar and "mighty hunter before the Lord" who built the Tower of Babel.

One of this novel's protagonists is asked to bring a copy of Victor Cherbuliez's Paule Mere to a party at Mrs. Walker's estate. The family courier Eugenio tries his best, but Randolph and his older sister continually come off as boorish Americans. Ultimately, the title character strolls around the Coliseum with the rakish Giovanelli, catches malaria, and dies, far away from her upstate New York home. Identify this novel narrated by Winterbourne, a story of a pretty young girl by Henry James.

Minor characters include the protagonist's tutor Wolfgang and friend Benno. Matthew Bourne's production used an entirely male cast, while many contemporary productions eliminate a portion written specifically for Pierina Legnani, namely the thirty-two fouettes danced by the female villain. That villain schemes with Baron Rothbart to separate the central prince and a denizen of the title location. Odette and Siegfried sink into the water at the end of what ballet by Tchaikovsky?

He celebrates "the love of Man and in praise of God" in the poem "In Country Heaven," while another poem conceives of his uncle's farm as "Adam and maiden." This author of the collections Eighteen Poems and Deaths and Entrances also wrote a radio play, Under Milk Wood, and the nostalgic "A Child's Christmas in Wales." name this Welsh poet of "Fern Hill" and "Do Not Go Gentle into That Good Night."

His family friend Phil Stone helped him publish an octosyllabic couplet verse sequence before he began writing novels like a satire on New Orleans in which Sherwood Anderson is caricatured as Dawson Fairchild. The sewing machine agent V. K. Ratliff appears in his Snopes trilogy, and he also wrote Mosquitoes and a novel in which Dilsey Gibson looks after the Compsons. Name this author of The Unvanquished, Light in August, Absalom, Absalom!, and The Sound and the Fury.

In one story, when his son is fatally bitten by a rattlesnake, this mythological character pleads for his life, only to be reminded that he had asserted previously that the dead should stay dead. In Wasco myth, he helps the Spirit Chief destroy Thunderbird. Prometheus-like, he steals fire from the mountain of the Fire Beings for humans, and he kicked a ball of mud to create the first man. Name this Native American trickster god and common wild animal of the Southwest.

The protagonist is laughed at for eating fish eyes, though much of his food is stolen by the kitchen staff. Fetyukov is broken, possibly because he refuses to follow Kuzyomin's "law of the taiga," which had saved the protagonist at Ust'-Izhma. Lieutenant Volkovoy makes workers remove clothing before going outside, but the title character remains somewhat stoical through eight years of hard labor. Name this work describing twenty four hours in the gulag, the first novel of Alexander Solzhenitsyn.
One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich

He discussed critics in the essay "A Moving Target" and novel The Paper Men. His other novels discuss early humans killing off Neanderthals, Edmund Talbot's journey to Australia, and a mariner's struggle to survive on a rock. In addition to those novels, The Inheritors, Rites of Passage, and Pincher Martin, he wrote a book based on R.M. Ballantyne's The Coral Island. A sow's head speaks to the kindly Simon in a book by what man, who created Ralph and Piggy in Lord of the Flies?

In a subplot of this novel, Miles Hendon attempts to claim the hand of Edith but finds that his brother Hugh has already married her. In the chapter "In Prison," two Baptists are burned at the stake. One title character grew up in Offal Court, and the other is taken to Southwark to join Hugo and his gang of thieves. That character proves his identity by revealing the royal seal to the Lord Protector. The beggar Tom Canty and Edward, the heir to the throne, reverse roles in what Mark Twain novel?

The figure founded the first Little Theater in America and helped to create the Institute for Juvenile Research. Before authoring the books Peace and Bread in Time of War and Democracy and Social Ethics, she took a trip to Europe with her friend Ellen Starr and, while in London, visited Toynbee Hall. That stopover inspired her to start a project on the corner of Polk and Halsted streets in Chicago. Identify this figure of the settlement-house movement who wrote Twenty Years at Hull House.

He died while visiting home to see a performance of his brother's play Prejudices. His orchestral works include the Capriccio Italien and the Marche Slave, while his ten operas include Iolanthe, Oprichnik, and three based on works of Pushkin, including Mazeppa and The Queen of Spades. Name this composer who used a quote from the Marseillaise and several cannons in a piece commemorating victory at Borodino, the 1812 Overture.

He ridiculed Joseph Priestley in his burlesque An Island in the Moon and attacked the conventional "creeping Jesus" in "The Everlasting Gospel." More representative work includes his America: A Prophecy and his descriptions of Orc and Urizen, part of the cosmology he created, in Visions of the Daughters of Albion. Identify this poet whose The Marriage of Heaven and Hell and Songs of Innocence and Experience contain such poems as "The Chimney Sweeper," "The Lamb," and "The Tiger."

Its second edition closes with a promise of rebirth in "The Voyage." Its cycle of Marie concludes with "To a Madonna" and Jeanne's poems include "The Jewels" and "The Vampire." "Landscape" and "The Swan" are found in the second section, Parisian Scenes, while its first section is Spleen and Ideal. Poems banned from its later printings were published separately as Les Épaves. Name this collection that revived the French sonnet after two hundred years, written by Charles Baudelaire.

A literary example of this is described as an idealistic schoolmaster in a novel by Edward Eggleston. Meredith Nicholson later used the term for a collective of homegrown authors including John James Piatt, George Ade, and James Whitcomb Riley. Some speculate that this term originated with a greeting, while others proffer that it is a corruption of the military term "hussar." such people as Calbert Cheaney, Richard Lugar, and Steve Alford might be known by what term used to identify residents of Indiana?

It opens with a history of Britain from the fall of Troy onward. One of the title characters enters carrying a sprig of holly on New Year's Day and issues a challenge that the other title character accepts, by means of the axe also carried into the hall. The challenge is completed a year later and exposed as a plan by Morgan le Fay to scare Guinevere to death. A girdle is established as a badge of honor by the Round Table in, what Pearl Poet work in which the mysterious challenger is Bercilak de Hautdesert?
Sir Gawain and the Green Knight

His addition of poems by philosopher T.E. Hulme to his collection Ripostes helped to spawn a certain literary movement. He did heavy editing on Eliot's The Waste Land and helped get William Carlos Williams and Hilda Doolittle published, and he even named his first poetry collection Hilda's Book. His longest work is often given the adjective "Pisan," referring to his time as a prisoner of war in Italy after being charged with treason by the Allies. Name this Imagist author of The Cantos.

His essays include "The Revolt of the Tartars" and a rumination on childhood, "The English Mail Coach." He attempted a study of dreaming in his treatise Suspiria de Profundis, but is likely better known for an 1822 work that begins with the protagonist's escape from Manchester Grammar School, describes the London prostitute Ann, and ends with visions of attacking tigers and a pain so profound that the narrator cries "I will sleep no more!" For 10 points identify this author of Confessions of an English Opium Eater.

Claude Mauriac's influence is seen in this man's novel Thirst for Love. He detailed the exploits of the young fisherman Shinji in The Sound of Waves and expressed his ideas about physical beauty in The Sailor Who Fell from Grace with the Sea. He also wrote a novel in which Mizoguchi burns down the title structure and a series about a recurring character who takes the forms of Isao Iinuma and Matsugae Kiyoaki. Name this author of The Temple of the Golden Pavilion and the Sea of Fertility tetralogy.

In this play, Faulkland is in love with Julia Melville, but is paranoid that she will meet with catastrophe. The climax takes place at King's Mead fields, where two of the title characters are set to fight a duel. Lucius O'Trigger eggs on Bob Acres, while Lydia is in love with the penniless Sir Beverley, whose true identity is Sir Jack Absolute. Identify this first play of Richard Brinsley Sheridan, featuring Lydia's idiom- butchering aunt, Mrs. Malaprop.

This author of The Fates of Famous Men was inspired by the court librarian Paulo de Perugina to write about mythological themes in Diana's Hunt and The Filostrato. The legend of Florio and Biancifiore is the basis of his Filcolo, and he also wrote a collection of one hundred stories, including "Tancred and the Golden Cup" and "Griselda." Those tales are told during a flight from the plague and were later ripped off in the Canterbury Tales. Name this Italian author of the Decameron.

The only convert in this play calls honor and dishonor opposites of the same stupidity and quotes Heine's poem on morphine. Pat and Ed Mosher are both parasites, Joe Mott wants to open a gambling house, and Cora and Chuck want to get married and move to New Jersey. Two Boer War veterans, the lawyer Willie Oban, and reporter Jimmy Tomorrow attempt to reform after a salesman kills his wife Evelyn because she had a "pipe dream." name this Eugene O'Neill play about Hickey, set at Harry Hope's tavern.

A sub-plot in this novel focuses on Sylvester Roberts, who transforms into the black nationalist Uhuru Simba. Mirza Saed's wife drowns in a river after Hal Valance attempts to exploit the hero's dreams. A visit to the "Hot Wax" nightclub causes the main character to lose the powers he received after falling from an exploding airplane into the English Channel. Name this novel about Saladin Chamcha and Gibreel Farishta, whose 1988 publication resulted in a fatwa being declared on Salman Rushdie.

This author of The Pentecost of Calamity and Romney popularized the white layer cake with his descriptions of socialite parties in his novel Lady Baltimore. His story Philosophy Four is based on his time at Harvard, where he met the dedicatee of a work subtitled "A Horseman of the Plains." In that novel, a man romances Molly Wood and engages in a duel with Trampas. Identify this author of Lin Maclean who saluted Theodore Roosevelt and created the Western novel in The Virginian.

In one of his plays, an awakening from a twenty-nine year sleep caused by encephalitis causes Deborah to suspect she has been enslaved. In a different play, Lulu lies down on a table while Stanley Webber plays a drum, and, in another, inexplicable food orders confuse Gus and Ben. His political works, such as One for the Road and Mountain Language, were a significant shift from his earlier absurdism. Name this author of A Kind of Alaska, The Caretakes, The Dumb Waiter, and The Birthday Party.

He developed poetry to read at meetings of Group 47 and published those poems as his first volume of work, Advantages of Wind-Fowl. Novels such as The Call of the Toad and The Flounder followed his story about the sleepwalking Roswitha Raguna, scarred Herbert Truczinski, and dwarf-by-choice Oskar Matzerath. Name this German author whose Dog Years and Cat and Mouse form the Danzig trilogy, along with The Tin Drum.

One of his works centers on Adam Salton's trip to Mercia and meeting with the sinister Lady March, while his first book was a collection of fairy tales, Under the Sunset. His The Lair of the White Worm and The Jewel of the 7 Stars turn on supernatural encounters, much like his most popular work, which features the use of a crucifix to draw a circle in the snow. For 10 points identify this author who created the characters Arthur Holmwood, Lucy Westenra, Mina Harker, and Van Helsing in the novel Dracula.

The last section of this man's major poem describes something "Everpresent," whispering "antiphonal in azure swing." He considers the clipper ships Rainbow and the Leander in "Cutty Sark" and evokes Pocahontas in "Powhatan's Daughter." He also alludes to Walt Whitman, who wrote about crossing a ferry underneath the same Brooklyn landmark that this poet wrote about. Name this author who used a stipend from Otto Kahn to write The Bridge.

He collaborated with John Nicolay on two monumental works on Abraham Lincoln and wrote editorials for the New York Tribune for five years. He also wrote Castilian Days and the poems in Illinois dialect, Pike County Ballads. He pushed hard at the 1898 Paris conference to retain the Philippines and signed namesake treaties with Pauncefote and Herran. Name this secretary of state under Theodore Roosevelt who negotiated the Panama Canal and formulated the Open Door policy.

Minor characters include the sensible Aunt Dinah, whose relationship with her coachman is ridiculed by everyone save the protagonist, and Didius, an irritating barrister of the church. Volume III discusses a treatise on noses, while Volume IX includes the tale of mad Maria, which resurfaces in the same author's A Sentimental Journey. Perhaps the most famous characters in the book are the pair of Parson Yorick and the narrator's Uncle Toby. For 10 points identify this unconventionally structured work by Laurence Sterne.
The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy, Gentleman

Among his posthumously published plays are The Earth Gods and Lazarus and His Beloved. After studying with Rodin in Paris, he moved to New York, where he founded the Al Magar newspaper and published such poetic works as The Madman. A novella by him is divided into such chapters as "Joy and Sorrow" and "Reason and Passion," and opens with the title character arriving in Orpahalese to spread his wisdom to the locals. Identify this Lebanese-American author of The Prophet.

His short stories are collected in The German Lieutenant and In Midsummer Days. His critical Letters to the Intimate Theatre provided the theoretical background for his plays To Damascus, The Pelican, and The Ghost Sonata. Another play of his tells the story of an upper-class woman who seduces her father's valet and then commits suicide. Identify this Swedish author of A Dance of Death and Miss Julie.

One of his dramas revolves around three years in the life of a black Louisville family, the Telfairs, while another turns on the struggle between the Greggs and the McEvoys. In addition to The Stonemason and The Gardener's Son, he described the depraved loner Lester Ballard in Child of God and wrote of the Glanton Gang in Blood Meridian. Name this author of Cities of the Plain and The Crossing who described John Grady Cole's journey to Mexico in All the Pretty Horses.

One of his books recounts the romance of Flora de Barral with a sketchy suitor. Another novel focuses on the tragedy that befalls the idealistic Razumov, and Captain MacWhirr navigates the Nan-Shan through a titular storm in his Typhoon. His first work deals with a structure that should have never been built, Almayer's Folly, and his other characters include a Chief Mate on the Patna and Mr. Verloc, who is The Secret Agent. Name this author of Lord Jim who wrote about Marlow and Kurtz in Heart of Darkness.

First published in Les Soirées de Médan, it tells of a group of travelers bound for Le Havre from Rouen. The title character is ignored by the group until they are stopped in a snow storm and only she has brought food, which she willingly shares. All is well until a Prussian officer stops the crew, refusing to let them pass unless Elisabeth Rousset sleeps with him. That is the plot of what short story by Guy de Maupassant, whose title is Elisabeth's nickname?

At one point in this work, the lawyer Wilson claims that John "Shadbelly" Billson's attempt to defraud was foiled because of the presence of the word "very," and Billson is exposed as a fraud along with the banker Pinkerton. Barclay Goodson is widely suspected as being the man who gave twenty dollars to a stranger, and Reverend Burgess's efforts to protect the Richards fail. The town motto becomes "Lead us into Temptation" after the civic reputation for honesty is destroyed. Name this Mark Twain story.

He taught Elizabethan literature and wrote the critical work Shakespeare and His Forerunners. He told of a tragic blood feud in "The Revenge of Hamish" and established himself by publishing Corn in Lippincott's Magazine, a work preceded by his Civil War novel Tiger-Lilies. Though born in Macon, Georgia, he was affiliated with Baltimore, where he wrote The Marshes of Glynn and performed in the Peabody Orchestra. Identify this author of The Song of the Chattahoochee.

This author chronicles the protagonist's songwriting ambitions and relationship with Vera in Seven Guitars; similarly to Schoolboy Barton's struggles, the protagonist searches out Martha after leaving the title character's chain gang in Joe Turner's Come and Gone. One character in his best known play believes himself to be the archangel Gabriel and opens the gates of heaven at the funeral of the main character, who used to play bas eball in the Negro Leagues, and counts his conflicts with his son Cory as "strikes." FTP, identify this author of The Pittsburgh Cycle, which includes Ma Rainey's Black Bottom and a play about Troy Maxson entitled Fences.

He closes his poem "From the Frontier of Writing" by leaving "posted soldiers flowing and receding like tree shadows into the polished windscreen" and finds the title berry to "take the roaming shape of Diogenes" in his collection The Haw Lantern, while he wrote about his father aging, contrasted with his earlier abilities with a horse-plough in "Follower." identify this poet who wrote about his four-year-old brother's death while he was at school in "Mid-Term Break" and promises that he will follow his father and grandfather by "Digging" the earth with his "squat pen," best known for his recent translation of Beowulf.

This person wrote about Ruth, Tommy, and Karen, who are clones raised for their body parts in his novel Never Let Me Go, while he also wrote about a propaganda painter in post-WWII Japan who must live with his shame in An Artist of the Floating World. For fifteen points, identify this British novelist who also wrote about the Butler Stevens in The Remains of the Day.

STRETCH ROUND This poet wrote three poems entitled "Material Cantos", which include "Hymn to Celery", Statute of Wine", and "Entrance Into Wood", which are included in his collection Residence on Earth. This poet wrote a series of odes to such diverse subjects as celery and lemons, and later wrote a cycle of love poems that ends with one that concludes "It is the hour of departure. Oh abandoned one." name this poet who wrote a poem about an Incan ruin entitled "The Heights of Macchu Picchu" and which was included in his Canto General, and who also wrote "Twenty Love Songs and a Song of Despair" and the "Elemental Odes.

This author wrote a play in which he adapted the Don Juan legend as one of his Four Little Tragedies. In one of this writer's long works, the title daughter of King Vladimir is captured by an evil creature, causing a knight to attempt to rescue her. Those works are The Stone Guest and Rustlan and Lyudmila. Identify this writer whose work was adapted by Modest Mussorgsky and who created a poem in which the title statue of Peter the Great comes to life and a drama in which a historical figure succeeds Dimitri Ivanovich, which are "The Bronze Horseman" and Boris Gudonov.

This author wrote a poem about a woman who was "ruined" and has "bright feathers", because "That's how you dress when you're ruined." In one poem by this author, he concludes that "these purblind Doomsters had as readily strown/ blisses about my pilgrimage as pain." In his last novel, Little Father Time hangs himself and Sue Brideshead's two children, and shortly thereafter the title character remarries Arabella Donn. In addition to "Hap" and Jude the Obscure, he wrote a novel about a man who auctions off his wife and child for five guineas and another in which the title character becomes another's mistress while her husband Angel is in Brazil, only to kill him upon Angel's return. Identify this author of The Mayor of Casterbridge and Tess of the d'Urbervilles.

In one story by this author a bird is described as "made with a jack- knife;" that story concerns the captain, the cook, the correspondent, and the oiler. In one short novel, the title character begins to date Pete, a bartender and her brother Jimmie's friend, and that novel opens with Jimmie, alone, representing Rum Alley in a fight with Devil's Row, while in his most famous work, he wrote of a regiment of "mule drivers" and "mud diggers" which includes the protagonist, who deserts it, rejoins it, and receives the title mark. The author of "The Open Boat" and Maggie: A Girl of the Streets who also wrote about Henry Fleming, identify this author of The Red Badge of Courage.

One novel written by an author from this nation features one character who falls in love with Margaret at Oxford, and another who marries a man who tries to pimp her to his boss. At the end of that novel, the latter has sex with the title character, a carpenter. In addition to The God of Small Things, a short story by another author from this nation features an ancient landlady who likes hearing her tenant call the moon landing "splendid." Besides "The Third and Final Continent," that author also wrote a novel about a boy who is given the name Gogol, The Namesake. Identify this nation, home to authors like Arundhati Roy and Jhumpa Lahiri.

One part of this work contains the often excerpted "Forest Murmurs," and one character in that part exhanges three riddles with the Wanderer. That part opens as that character, Mime, is forging a sword. One of this work's two ensemble pieces comes after its namesakes mock an ugly character who tries to woo them; he then steals what they are guarding. That piece is the song of Woglinde, Wellgunde, and Flosshilde, the Rhinemaidens, and that ugly character is the dwarf Alberich, who has stolen the Rheingold. Ending with the section entitled Twilight of the Gods, its second section contains a piece in which four of Brunnhilde's sisters gather near a mountain, the famous "Ride of the Valkyries." identify this set of four operas by Richard Wagner.

One of this author's plays features a President who wants to marry his son to the Duke's concubine, but Ferdinand is more interested in the daughter of the town musician. That play was originally entitled Luisa Miller, while another play concerns the Prince of Asturias, Don Carlos. In another play, one coldly rational son is complemented by his hotheaded brother, who befriends Scooter and Schweitzer and is opposed by Spiegelberg, one of the title characters; at one point the character is believed dead, prompting Amalia to sing the Hektorlied. The title character of another work blocks his antagonist's path to Kussnacht. Identify this author of a play about Franz and Karl Moor, as well as one about Gessler's tyranny in Switzerland, the author of The Robbers and William Tell.

In this novel, the death of one character occurs after performing an autopsy on a local peasant who had died of typhus, and after attending a ball, two characters in this work travel to Abdotya Stepanovna's estate, Nikolskoe, where Madame Odintsova also lives. In this novel, two characters eventually marry Fenichka and Katya, while Pavel is shot in the leg during a duel. Centering on Arkady Kirsanov and Evgeny Bazarov, name this novel by Ivan Turgenev which introduced Nihilism.

One of this man's works is a narrative written by the young man from the banquet scene from Stages on Life's Way. That work was examined by Lacan in The Four Fundamental Concepts of Psychoanalysis and is entitled Repetition. Another work by this philosopher contains the legend of Agnes and the merman and contains the problema "Is there a teleological suspension of the ethical." In addition to Fear and Trembling, he used pseudonyms like Victor Eremita and Judge Vilhelm while considering the aesthetic life, which requires a sort of "crop rotation," in contrast to another option, the ethical life. Identify this author of Either/Or.

In the first scene of the play she appears in, this character is compared to a "white ewe" by a man who tells her father that "the devil will make a grandsire of" him. Her tears are described as creating crocodiles from the earth in a scene in which she is defended by Lodovico after being struck. Her mother's maid Barbary had a "song of ‘willow'", which this character sings to her own attendant. This character offers a man with a headache a handkerchief, which is picked up by Emilia, then used to frame Cassio. Identify this daughter of Brabantio who gets smothered by a pillow by the title character of the play she appears in, Shakespeare's Othello.

Henri de Marsay falls in love with Paquita Valdes in this author's novel The Girl with the Golden Eyes, while Lucien de Rubempré appears in both Lost Illusions and The Harlot High and Low. The Maiso Vaquere is the residence of the titular character of this author's novel Father Goriot, and this author also wrote Cousin Bette. Raphael de Valentin puts on the titular garment in this author's novel The Wild Ass's Skin. Identify this author best known for his huge multivolume work The Human Comedy, a French novelist.

Another author from this country wrote The Place Without Limits and about Humerto Pinaloza whose personality disintegrates in his novel The Obscene Bird of Night. Along with Jose Donoso, Robert Bolano set a novel By Night in this place. Perhaps the best known author from this country wrote Eva Luna, Of Love and Shadows, and about the psychic Trueba family in her novel The House of the Spirits. Identify this country which is home to writers like Isabel Allende.

This author wrote about a man who has an affair with Anna during a trip to Yalta. He also wrote about a lawyer who takes up an offer to imprison himself for 15 years, while in another story a man describes his brother who fulfils his dream of consuming the title fruit even though they are sour and unripe. In addition to "Lady with the Lapdog," "The Bet," and "Gooseberries," he wrote about Nina who ignores Konstantin's advances which leads Konstantin to commit suicide. Identify this author of The Seagull, who also wrote The Cherry Orchard.

In one scene in this play, the second of title characters draw black crosses from a helmet, while Yvette is a prostitute who seduces a Colonel and attempts to purchase the first title character's possession. At the beginning of one scene, the first title character sings "The Song of the Great Capitulation." In another scene, a mute girl climbs on a rooftop and loudly beats a drum to warn a village of an advancing army, and one of that character's siblings is executed for stealing a money box. Featuring the siblings Kattrin, Eilif, and Swiss Cheese, identify this work in which Anna Fierling lugs around a canteen during the Thirty Years war, written by Bertolt Brecht.

In one of his plays Henry Carr participates in a production of The Importance of Being Earnest which is managed by James Joyce, while Moon and Birdboot learn that Puckeridge is actually the title character in another of his play. In addition to Travesties and The Real Inspector Hound, he wrote a play in which Bernard Nightingale declares that Lord Byron murderd Ezra Chater as Thomasina is tutored by Septimus Hodge, and his most famous play sees the title character toss a coin several times only to see it show heads. Identify this author of Arcadia and Rosencrantz and Guildenstern are Dead.

In one episode in this novel, two men pretend to be the dead Peter Wilks' brothers to steal their inheritance, while in another the protagonist has a moral crisis about concealing stolen property before lying to a group of men that his father has smallpox. Later, he gets caught up in a family feud between the Shephardsons and the Grangerfords and is saved by his travelling companion, who had repaired the raft. The story's finale is set into motion by two con men, the duke and dauphin, who sell Jim to Silas and Sally Phelps. Name this novel written by Mark Twain in which the title character is misidentified as Tom Sawyer.

In this work, a man suffering from infertility is forced to promise asylum without knowing why he must provide it, and it begins with a lament by a Nurse wishing that a trip had never been made. The final scene of this play, which traditionally features an exit on a dragon chariot to the safety of Aegus's court, was retooled by Robinson Jeffers in a famous adaptation. A pair of robes alternately poison or immolate Glauce and her father Creon, who had hoped to banish the title character after installing her husband on the throne. Ending with the title character's murder of her own children, identify this Euripides play that sees the wrath wrought on Corinth by the spurned wife of Jason.

In one poem, this man declared that "the fact is the sweetest dream that labor knows", while the title figure of another "says the highway dust is over all." In addition to "Mowing" and "The Oven Bird", he wrote a poem which sees a heartbeat fade to "nothing – Gone!" and one which notes that "Eden sank to grief", "Out, Out" and "Nothing Gold Can Stay". This author of "Fire and Ice" noted that "The land was ours before we were the land's" in another poem. Identify this author of "The Gift Outright" who included the refrain "Good fences make good neighbors" in "Mending Wall" and also wrote "The Road Not Taken" and "Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening."

A quote from this play that begins "Thou has nor youth nor age" was used as the epigraph for T.S. Eliot's Gerontion. The beginning of Act IV, scene 3 sees a clown helping the hangman Abhorson prepare for the execution of the criminal Barnardine, who is eventually pardoned. Some comic relief is provided when Froth and Pompey are arrested at Mrs. Overdone's brothel by Constable Elbow. At this play's end, Luci's life is spared and the Duke orders Mariana to marry another character. Identify this play in which Isabella returns from a nunnery to save her condemned brother Claudio from the cruel deputy Angelo, a work of William Shakespeare.

TRASH This character clips off a bit of his dead father's ear at his funeral in order to prove paternity and sticks a knife into an electrical socket to see what would happen if he died. This character overdoses on Alzheimer's drugs in order to reach memories of Amber even though she is dating Wilson, and Alison Cameron is infatuated with this character during the first three seasons. Overseen by Lisa Cuddy and Head of Diagnostic Medicine at Princeton- Plainsborough Hospital, identify this character, a doctor on a namesake television show played by Hugh Laurie.

LITERATURE One character in this work is described as a "duck shaped woman" and One character in this work is revealed to have been illegitimately fathered by the preacher, Whitfield, while another character is tricked into having sex as a means of abortion, Dewey Dell. Another character describes his mother as "a fish," Vardaman, while Darl is put in an insane asylum for attempting to burn down a barn containing his mother's corpse. Identify this novel about the Bundren family's journey to bury their matriarch by William Faulkner.

Social Science: This author discussed the "meaning of meaning it" and psychoanalyzed the titular religious figure in Young Man Luther and devised a scale which drew distinctions like trust v. Mistrust and industry v. Inferiority. For 15 points, identify this psychologist, author of Childhood and Society, who created an eight staged model of development and the term "identity crisis".

S LIT This author praised the "unseen power" that "floats unseen among us" in one work and told of Laon and Cythna 's revolution against the Ottoman empire in another. In addition to "Hymn to Intellectual Beauty" and "The Revolt of Islam," this author of A Defense of Poetry described the title entity as the "breath of Autumn's being" in a work in terza rima and wrote another poem about a "king of kings" who commands all to "look upon my works, ye mighty, and despair. "name this author of "Ode to the West Wind," "To a Skylark," and "Ozymandius."

Weekend of Quizbowl Saturday Tournament 2009 Round 3 RTB (2/2 Hist, 2/2 Sci, 1/1 Lit, 1/1 RMP, 1/1 SS, 1/1 Arts) In one of this author's works, John Goldencalf meets four talking monkeys, while his first novel ended with the marriage of Emily Moseley to the Earl of Pendennyss. In addition to The Monikins and Precaution, he wrote a novel about Richard Barnstable, the commander of the Ariel, called The Pilot. His "Literary Offenses" were enumerated in a Mark Twain essay that criticized the unrealism of some of his characters, who include Chingachgook and a man called "Pathfinder". Identify this author whose novels about Natty Bumppo were collected in his Leatherstocking Tales, which also included his The Last of the Mohicans.

One scene near the end of this work, several days after its protagonist buys some overripe strawberries, sees Jasiu win a fight. This work's protagonist encounters a pair of clerks from Pola accompanied by a man with dyed hair and rouged cheeks, who resembles a traveler he'd encountered in a cemetery and a Charon-esque character who warned that protagonist "You will pay." Its protagonist ignores warnings to leave Lido Beach and dies due to a cholera epidemic sweeping through the title city. Identify this work in which the 15-year-old Tadzio is the obsession of Gustav von Aschenbach, written by Thomas Mann.

On "dragon mountains" or "barrier of spears"] Stretch Round (2/2 Hist, 2/2 Sci, 2/2 Lit, 1/1 Arts, 1/1 RMP) This author asked "What is the meter of the dictionary?" in the title poem of a series of sonnets following "the long world's gentleman", Altarwise by Owl Light. He noted that "Dead men naked they shall be one" in a poem titled after its repeated refrain, "And death shall have no dominion." "Ceremony after a Fire Raid" was among the poems included in his collection Deaths and Entrances, the final poem of which saw him singing "in chains like the sea". Identify this author of "Fern Hill" and the radio play Under Milk Wood, who advocated raging "against the dying of the light" in "Do Not Go Gentle Into that Good Night".

This character was once wounded while fighting Asteropaeus, and one story about him claims that after his death he was revived and worshipped on Leuke. He once healed the king of Mysia after previously wounding that monarch, Telephus, in a battle. His charioteer Automedon drove his horses, the mortal Pedasos and the immortal Balius and Xanthus. This figure fatally punched Thersites in the face in retaliation for laughing after this man had killed Penthesilea, and he fought and killed Memnon after Memnon had killed his companion Antilochus. Identify this father of Neoptolemus and companion of Patroclus who, in the Iliad, is killed by Paris after himself killing Hector.

The protagonist of this work considers a curse he laid fulfilled when Uiko and her deserter boyfriend die in a murder-suicide, and that protagonist once enviously scratched a cadet's scabbard. Its protagonist receives two cartons of cigarettes for stomping on a pregnant woman at the behest of a soldier and later watches a woman put her breast milk into a cup of tea. Tsurukawa commits suicide after earlier abandoning its protagonist at Otani University, where he befriends the clubfooted Kashiwagi. Identify this work in which Mizoguchi becomes obsessed with the title structure and eventually sets fire to it, a novel by Yukio Mishima.
The Temple of the Golden Pavilion

Based on a John Luther Long short story, Act II of this work ends with a group of characters singing the wordless "Coro a bocca chiusa", or "Humming Chorus". Its main male character, a spinto tenor, details his "intoxication" in the aria "Amore o grillo" before laying out his wandering philosophy in "Dovunque al mondo". Its title character reads the inscription on her father's knife and sings "Con onor muore" before killing herself, though she'd earlier dreamed of the male lead's return in "Un bel di, vedremo". Identify this opera in which Prince Yamadori is refused by Cio Cio San, who herself is stood up by Pinkerton, a work of Giacomo Puccini.

Maria Iribarne is stalked and murdered by Juan Pablo Castel in one work from this country's literary history, The Tunnel. A politician from this country described the life of Juan Quiroga in a work subtitled "Civilization and Barbarism," Facundo. This home of and Ernesto Sabato and Domingo Sarmiento also produced the creator of W218 in Pubis Angelical and Molina and Valentin in Kiss of the Spider Woman, Manuel Puig, and the author of Hopscotch, Julio Cortazar. Richard Madden hunts the spy Yu Tsun in "The Garden of the Forking Paths," which appears in a collection that also includes "The Library of Babel," Ficciones, written by another native author. Name this South American country, home to Jorge Luis Borges.

One character in this novel is known as The Avenger and is attacked by the protagonist after he is offered a roll for breakfast. At one point in this work, the protagonist joins an expensive club where boys eat fancy dinners and argue about debts known as "Finches of the Grove." Early on in this novel, the protagonist frees a convict by the name of Abel Magwitch who later becomes his benefactor and sends him to London. There, he becomes a companion of the young Estella who is being raised by the wicked Miss Havisham to take revenge on men. Identify this novel by Charles Dickens that involves rising-up in society of the former orphan Pip Pirrup.

Literature: This author, who appears as Lewis Brogan in Simone de Beauvoir's The Mandarins, told of Dove Linkhorn's "three rules of life" in A Walk on the Wild Side and examined Hemingway in Notes from a Sea Diary. For fifteen points, name this American who created Frankie Machine in The Man with the Golden Arm.

An Italian scholar is taken prisoner by a strange doppelganger named Hoja in an Orhan Pamuk novel named after a white one of these, while a blue on titles a work about Valancy Stirling by Lucy Montgomery.. Theodore of Falconara appears in a work titled for one of these, which sees Manfred attempt to wed Isabella after his son Conrad is crushed by a giant, ghostly helmet. That work by Horace Walpole, considered the first Gothic novel, is named after one of these at Otranto. A work named for one of these sees the protagonist encounter Pepi, Jeremiah, Erlanger, and Freida while trying in vain to find the bureacrat Klamm. Identify these structures, one of which K. Tries to enter in a Kafka novel, which also appear in literature through examples like Camelot.

Twenty children join a hunt for an insect, which a boy hands over to a girl in this man's short story "The Grasshopper and the Bell Cricket." Eguchi sleeps next to the title figures for seven nights in his "The House of the Sleeping Beauties," and this man also wrote a work about a match between Otake and Shūsai. Author of The Master of Go, he wrote a novel opening with a tea ceremony, and another in which Shimamura has an affair with the geisha Komako in a hot spring town. Name this Japanese author of Thousand Cranes and Snow Country.

A headmaster draws female genitalia on a blackboard in this man's play Two Ears, Two Weddings. His poetry is collected in Monologues, and he himself narrates his novels Slowness and Immortality. In one work by this author, "Long Live Trotsky!" is written on a postcard sent by Ludvik Jahn to a girl. Author of The Joke and The Book of Laughter and Forgetting, he wrote a work about Sabina's affair with the husband of the photographer Tereza, the surgeon Tomáš. Name this Czech author of The Unbearable Lightness of Being.

One character by this author tells Charlie Morris that "it would make everything infinitely easier" if he hated white men. Tshembe Matoseh appeared in this author's posthumously completed Les Blancs, and she wrote of Hannibal's attempt at a slave revolt in The Drinking Gourd. In one work, she wrote of the homosexual David and the title character's wife Iris, The Sign in Sidney Brustein's Window, as well as the play To Be Young, Gifted, and Black. Name this author who created Travis and Walter Younger in her A Raisin in the Sun.

"Plainer myrtle pleases" the speaker of one of his poems who detests the titular "Persian Fopperies." This man wrote "To Chloë" and Epodes, and proposed the restoration of pantheon-worship in his Carmen Saeculare. In one work, he compares the title entity to painting and discusses "in medias res," and his Satirae I and II contain eighteen poems of his namesake satire altogether. Penner of the lines "carpe diem" and "dulce et decorum est pro patria mori," name this ancient Roman poet of the Ars Poetica.

He wrote about a drunk man who was cut down from hanging himself by his niece in a story where a bar manager closes down early to see his wife. In another work of his, Al and Max look for the ex-fighter Ole Anderson. In addition to A Clean, Well Lighted Place and The Killers, which features Nick Adams, he wrote about Pedro San Roman, who has an affair with Lady Brett Ashley, and another novel about Robert Jordan blowing up a bridge in the Spanish Civil War. Name this author of The Sun Also Rises and For Whom the Bell Tolls.

In this play's parabasis, the chorus recommends this play get the highest awards and insults the audience for having spurned it. The main character drives away Pasias and Amynias after they attempt to collect the debt his son built up from being lazy and spending it on horse races, and at the end of the play that man burns his former teacher's home. Sending his son Pheiddippides to learn new logic, the main character Strepsiades is kicked out of the Thinkery, a sophist school. Name this play by Aristophanes that lampoons Socrates.

He opened one work with "Heard by the soul, footsteps / in the mind more than shadows" and he wrote on Whorf's "linguistic relativity" in his essay "Reading and Contemplation," collected in Convergences. In addition to A Draft of Shadows and The Bow and the Lyre, this author repeated the first six lines of one of his poems at the conclusion to make it cyclical, and he wrote about the Southwestern American pachucos who are in limbo between their native culture before he studies fiestas and other Mexican culture. Name this author of a poem representing the Aztec calendar, Sun Stone, along with The Labyrinth of Solitude.

In one of his works king Ceyx is the drowned husband of the despairing Lady Alcyon, and the idealized woman White in that work represents Blanche of Lancaster. One of his works includes the story of Arveragus, who marries Dorigen, and one includes a dream about a goose, a turtledove, and other birds meeting to discuss love. Along with The Book of the Duchess and A Parlement of Foules this man wrote a work where a knight searches for what women truly want, among other stories told at the Tabard Inn. Name this author of tales by the wife of Bath and the Nun's Priest, The Canterbury Tales.

He wrote gacelas "of the Dark Death" and "of Unforseen Love" in his collection Divan. This author names an Albee play, and he wrote a poem about a black man using a spoon to gouge out crocodile eyes in "The King of Harlem." He wrote about a barren woman married to Juan who visits a witch to try and conceive, and in another play Angustias, Poncia, and Adela are the repressed daughters of the title character. An unnamed bridegroom kills Leonardo in the other play in this author's Rural Trilogy. Name this author of Yerma, The House of Bernarda Alba, and Blood Wedding.

In one of this author's novels, the unnamed narrator and her boyfriend Joe spend a week on the island where her father used to live, and another of her novels has Simon Jordan investigate a historical murder. In addition to Surfacing and Alias Grace, she won the 2000 Booker Prize for a book in which Iris Chase attributes a novel to her dead sister, The Blind Assassin, but her most famous novel concerns Offred's life in the dystopian Gilead. Name this Canadian author of The Handmaid's Tale.

In one of his plays, Xerxes angers the gods after building a bridge that spans the Hellespont, and another play begins with Kratos, Bia, and Hephaestus in the Caucasus. Athena changes the name of the Furies after a jury in The Eumenides, which follows this author's The Libation Bearers in a trilogy which sees the vengeance its namesake takes on Aegisthus and his mother Clytemnestra. Name this Ancient Greek playwright who wrote The Persians and Prometheus Bound and began his Oresteia with Agamemnon.

When one character in this play is revealed to be in the biology instead of the math department, another character accuses him of wanting to genetically engineer a super race. That character had written a novel about a boy who kills his parents but can't convince his father-in-law, the head of the university, to publish it. The central couple invents a child they never had and kills him off in a car accident. Bringing Up Baby, Humiliate the Host, and Hump the Hostess are "games" invented by George and Martha to entertain Nick and Honey. Name this Edward Albee play.

At the end of this novel one character sets about restoring his estate at Bald Hills and another character is married to the gold-digger Helene who kills herself in an overdose. Andrey becomes engaged to a character who attempts to elope with Anatole Kuragin and is the brother of Nicholas Rostov who distinguishes himself in the same unit as Pierre Bezhukov at the Battle of Borodino. Name this novel set against Napoleon's invasion of Russia, written by Leo Tolstoy.

In this work, a fable about a gatekeeper and a man who waits his entire life outside the gate is told to the protagonist in a cathedral after he has received assistance from the merchant Rudi Block and the painter Titorelli. Jealousy arises when the protagonist believes Montag and Captain Lanz are conspiring, shortly after he steals a kiss with Fraulein Burstner, while the protagonist's sexual encounter with Leni results in reduced aid from Herr Hudd, a lawyer. Name this Franz Kafka novel about Josef K, a banker who is arrested and executed for an unknown crime.

In one work by this man, the protagonist is taken to frog-plagued Arnewi as well as the Wariri village of King Dahfu by his guide Romilayu, while another work by this man is narrated by "Chick" and tells of a Parisian professor in love with Nikki who leaves the country when he comes down with AIDS. In addition to Henderson the Rain King and Ravelstein, this man wrote a work which centers on a twice-divorced man from Ludeyville who writes dozens of letters without sending them, while another features the creator of Von Trenck, Charlie Citrine, who is a manifestation of the author. Identify this Chicago writer of Herzog and Humboldt's Gift.

After being told that he is in trouble from the government for attempting to sell a city to the Turks, one character in this work hides in a turtle shell to escape detection. The aforementioned Sir Politic Would Be is duped by Peregrine, while Corvino is forced to wear donkey ears in public, Corbaccio is forced to forfeit his property and the title character is put in prison. Set in Venice and revolving around the faked death of the title character and the parasite Mosca's attempt to gain his wealth, name this Ben Jonson play about the titular "fox".

If you're an Archfederalist) An early story by this author sees the protagonist renewing an affair with Hilda Trevelyan before dying as his titular structure collapses. Besides Alexander's Bridge, this author penned a novel where musician Clement Sebastian hires Haverford-native Lucy Gayheart to be his accompanist, as well as a novel whose middle book is devoted to Tom Outland's solitary life on Blue Mesa in The Professor's House. More famous stories include one about the Bergsons and Jean Marie Latour in New Mexico. She also told of Jim Burden's affection for Lena Lingard and the titular Bohemian immigrant in a well regarded 1918 novel. FTP, identify this prairie novelist of O, Pioneers! And My Antonia.

One character in this novel has a bad relationship with his drunken wife, falls in love with Rachel, and asks his boss for help to escape his life; his name is Stephen Blackpool. Mrs. Sparsit is a housekeeper employed by one of the central characters of this novel, and she hopes to marry him. A student named Blitzer in this novel is asked to give a description of a horse, which he accomplishes perfectly, and most of it is set in Coketown. Identify this novel about Josiah Bounderby's marriage to Louisa Gradgrind, the daughter of Thomas who runs a school that teaches facts and only facts, which was written by Charles Dickens.

This writer collaborated with Antonio Coello to write The Prodigy of Germany. The author of Devotion to the Cross and The Mighty Magician, this writer also wrote the plays The Painter of his Dishonor and The Surgeon of his Honor. Basilio, the King of Poland, imprisons his son Seigismundo in one play by this writer, while in another, a soldier rapes the title character's daughter; that character's name is Crespo. Identify this dramatist who wrote Life is a Dream and The Mayor of Zalamea, a Spaniard.

One work by this author sees the Dancing, Music, Philosophy and Fencing Masters get into a fight over whose discipline is the best, and in another a man is beaten until he is convinced he can cure Lucinde's sudden muteness. A character boasts of translating Roman history into limericks in this author's The Affected Damsels. Besides authoring a 5-act version of Don Juan, one of his most famous works hinges on a confusion over the name of Arnolphe, a man who intends to marry Agnes. Argan undergoes frequent enemas and tries to marry his daughter to a doctor in his The Imaginary Invalid. Name this French comedic playwright who penned The Miser, School for Wives, The Misanthrope, and Tartuffe.

One character in this novel sees a Bible with verses marked out for travelling salesmen to use for differing occasions, which depresses him. This novel begins with a depiction of a dentist who cannot get enough money to return to England named Tench. The protagonist of this novel had a daughter named Brigitta with a woman named Maria, the sin of which he can't repent. Identify this novel about an unnamed whiskey priest in repressive Mexico, a novel by Graham Greene whose name refers to the Lord's Prayer.

In 2002 a 220-pound statue of the title character of this short story was stolen in St. Petersburg. That character is first found in a roll by a barber named Ivan, whose wife thinks he has harmed someone to get it. Eventually the reader learns it left of its own accord from a man named Kovalev, who observes it in the fancy dress of a civil servant before it returns to him. FTP name this Nikolai Gogol short story about a missing item from Kovalev's face.
